LESSON: ORAL LITERATURE 6.1.1 SONGS/ ORAL POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Oral Literature 6.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 6.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do play songs help in social cohesion in the society? 2. How do lullabies portray family relationships?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Literature 6.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner brainstorms, sings and engages in various activities

with the peers.

● Learning to learn: This is developed as the learner relates learning to real life as they brainstorm on the play songs

and lullabies that they have heard or sang in the past and present in class.

● Respect: This is nurtured as the learner appreciates the contribution of peers during discussions and presentations on

● Love: This is enhanced as the learner shares responses from discussion on the structure and features lullabies and
